hook: OpenAI just raised what it pays hackers who find security holes in its systems. The headline is "Rewarding defenders with bigger bug bounties." Most small business owners skip this kind of update. It reads like it's for engineers.
body:
OpenAI just raised what it pays hackers who find security holes in its systems. The headline is "Rewarding defenders with bigger bug bounties."

Most small business owners skip this kind of update. It reads like it's for engineers.

It isn't. If you run ads, you log into Meta, Google, maybe a CRM, every single day. Every password you reuse, every "stay logged in" you click, is a door. Bigger bounties mean more skilled people are hunting for cracks in the tools you already trust — which tells you plainly how much those doors are worth to someone else.

You don't need to understand the code. You need three minutes: turn on two-factor login, where a password alone isn't enough to get in, on your ad accounts and your email. That one habit protects more of your business than most of what gets taught about running ads.

Nobody tells you this because it doesn't sell anything. It just keeps what you've built from disappearing one Tuesday morning.

slides.text: OpenAI just started paying hackers more to break its own systems.
This looks like news for engineers. It is actually about your login page.
A bug bounty pays outsiders to find security holes before criminals do.
OpenAI just raised what it pays them. That tells you something.
When the reward for breaking in goes up, so does the number of people trying.
Your ad account, your inbox, your CRM all sit behind one password most days.
Meta and Google already give you a free second lock on every account.
Most people never turn it on. Here is where it lives.
items: Meta: Settings → Security and Login → Two-Factor Authentication

slides.text: One missed step and a hacked ad account can drain a budget before you even see the alert.

slides.text: The bigger bounty isn't the story. The fact that someone is always trying is.
Turn on two-factor login today. It takes three minutes and costs nothing.
